meta.descripcion: Bank of complex English words, with an easy-read meaning and a real-life example. Own content (not a translation of content/dictionary/es.json — see doc/en/I18N.md §3).
meta.fuente: Words chosen from CEFR C1/C2 advanced English vocabulary lists (esl-lounge, Espresso English, Cambridge word lists). Definitions and examples written from scratch in easy-read style for Apptonomia, not copied from any source.
meta.estado: Standalone content bank, not yet wired into any activity. tools/dictionary/data.js holds the subset already used by the Dictionary activity (24 words); this file is a broader base for that or future activities.

campos.definition: easy-read meaning: short sentence, one idea
campos.example: example sentence in a real adult-life context

words.definition: Costs an amount you can pay without trouble.
words.example: This flat is affordable: it costs less than others nearby.

words.definition: Easy to use, at a good time or place.
words.example: The bus stop is convenient: it's right outside my house.

words.definition: Something you can trust, it does not fail.
words.example: This watch is reliable: it always shows the right time.

words.definition: Can change easily to fit new needs.
words.example: My work schedule is flexible, I can choose my hours.

words.definition: Lasts a long time without breaking.
words.example: These boots are durable: I've worn them for three years.

words.definition: Done carefully, checking every part.
words.example: She did a thorough check before signing the papers.

words.definition: Useful and simple, without extra trouble.
words.example: This bag is practical: everything fits inside it.

words.definition: Easy to reach or use for everyone.
words.example: The ramp makes the entrance accessible for wheelchairs.

words.definition: Just the right amount, enough for what is needed.
words.example: We have sufficient food for the whole week.

words.definition: Lasts only for a short time.
words.example: We're living in a temporary flat until ours is fixed.

words.definition: Happens little by little, not all at once.
words.example: The change in schedule was gradual, a bit each week.

words.definition: Done suddenly, without planning ahead.
words.example: The trip was spontaneous: we decided that same morning.

words.definition: Useful for many different things.
words.example: This tool is versatile: it works for several jobs.

words.definition: Not too much and not too little, balanced.
words.example: He spent a moderate amount on the trip.

words.definition: Arrives at the exact time, not late or early.
words.example: She was punctual: she arrived right at nine.

words.definition: Can really be done, it is possible.
words.example: The plan is feasible if we start this week.

words.definition: Real, not a copy or a fake.
words.example: That painting is a genuine Picasso.

words.definition: Clean and in order, everything in its place.
words.example: He kept his room tidy every day.

words.definition: Not required, you can choose it or not.
words.example: Dessert is optional; you don't have to have it.

words.definition: Something done the same way, again and again.
words.example: Putting away the shopping is a routine task at home.

words.definition: Makes sense and is not too much.
words.example: The ticket price seemed reasonable to me.

words.definition: Can be known before it happens.
words.example: The rain was predictable: the forecast said so this morning.

words.definition: Makes you feel good, without any trouble.
words.example: This armchair is very comfortable for watching TV.

words.definition: Needs to be done now, it cannot wait.
words.example: The call was urgent: there was a problem at work.

words.definition: Done because someone wants to, not because they're forced.
words.example: Helping at the food bank is voluntary work.

words.definition: Sees the good side of things.
words.example: He's optimistic: he believes everything will turn out fine.

words.definition: Sees the bad side of things.
words.example: She's pessimistic: she thinks something will go wrong.

words.definition: Likes to share what they have with others.
words.example: He was generous: he gave away half of his lunch.

words.definition: Doesn't boast about what they have or do.
words.example: She's humble: she never talks about her awards.

words.definition: Acts fast, without thinking first.
words.example: He was impulsive: he bought the car without checking the price.

words.definition: Thinks carefully before acting, to avoid problems.
words.example: She was cautious: she looked both ways before crossing.

words.definition: Wants to learn new things all the time.
words.example: He's curious: he always asks how things work.

words.definition: Recovers well after something hard happens.
words.example: She was resilient: she tried again after the failure.

words.definition: Prefers to be alone or with few people.
words.example: He's introverted: he likes staying home reading.

words.definition: Enjoys being around people and talking a lot.
words.example: She's outgoing: she knows everyone at the party.

words.definition: Feels emotions easily.
words.example: He's sensitive: he cries watching sad films.

words.definition: Feels sorry for others' pain and wants to help.
words.example: She was compassionate: she helped the man who had fallen.

words.definition: Doesn't forget or forgive when they've been hurt.
words.example: He's resentful: he's still angry about something from a year ago.

words.definition: Treats people well, friendly when talking.
words.example: The neighbour is affable: he always says hello with a smile.

words.definition: Helps others without expecting anything back.
words.example: She was selfless: she gave money without telling anyone.

words.definition: Doesn't easily believe what others say.
words.example: He's distrustful: he asks several times before believing something.

words.definition: Shows a lot of excitement about something.
words.example: She's enthusiastic about the new job: she arrives happy every day.

words.definition: Won't change their mind even when told they're wrong.
words.example: He was stubborn: he kept his plan even though everyone warned him.

words.definition: Likes to help other people.
words.example: He's helpful: he always helps carry the bags.

words.definition: Can be hurt easily, needs protection.
words.example: Older people are more vulnerable to the cold.

words.definition: Says what they think with respect, without fear.
words.example: She was assertive: she said she didn't like the plan without getting angry.

words.definition: Feels a soft, quiet sadness, like missing something.
words.example: He felt wistful looking at old photos.

words.definition: Happy and in a good mood most of the time.
words.example: Grandma is cheerful: she's always laughing and telling stories.

words.definition: Feels worried or nervous about something that might happen.
words.example: She felt anxious before the job interview.

words.definition: Thinks about how their actions affect others.
words.example: He's considerate: he always asks before turning up the music.

words.definition: A block of time a person works.
words.example: Her shift starts at eight in the morning.

words.definition: A paper that states the terms of a job or agreement.
words.example: He signed the contract before starting work.

words.definition: The money someone earns for working.
words.example: She gets her wage on the last day of the month.

words.definition: The money you plan to spend on something.
words.example: We made a budget for the holiday.

words.definition: Money paid to the government by law.
words.example: Taxes help pay for hospitals and schools.

words.definition: A set of rules that must be followed.
words.example: The regulation says you must wear a helmet on a bike.

words.definition: A series of steps to get something done officially.
words.example: Getting an ID card is a procedure at the office.

words.definition: An official paper asking for something.
words.example: She filled in the application to ask for the grant.

words.definition: A group set up to do something, like a company or charity.
words.example: The bank is an organization that keeps money safe.

words.definition: A group of people who live in, or share, the same place.
words.example: The whole community helped clean the park.

words.definition: Making sure everyone can take part, leaving no one out.
words.example: The ramp improves inclusion for wheelchair users.

words.definition: Treating a person worse because they are different.
words.example: The law forbids discrimination based on where a person is from.

words.definition: Being able to do things yourself, without others' help.
words.example: Cooking alone gives him more independence.

words.definition: A large organization, like the town hall or a hospital.
words.example: The town hall is an institution in the town.

words.definition: The right and duty to live as part of a country.
words.example: Voting is part of citizenship.

words.definition: The set of laws in a country.
words.example: Legislation protects workers' rights.

words.definition: A message telling people about something coming up, like a course.
words.example: The notice for the new course was posted.

words.definition: Money given by the government to help do something.
words.example: The group got a grant for the workshop.

words.definition: Organizing and running the tasks of something well.
words.example: They share the management of the household money.

words.definition: The built things a place needs to work, like roads or water.
words.example: The village improved its infrastructure with a new road.

words.definition: Can be kept going over time without causing harm.
words.example: Riding a bike is sustainable transport.

words.definition: Work together with others to get something done.
words.example: Everyone cooperated to organize the party.

words.definition: The person who speaks for a group.
words.example: The residents' representative spoke at the meeting.

words.definition: Doing things in a clear way, without hiding anything.
words.example: The club explained with transparency where the money goes.

words.definition: Made up of many different kinds of people or things.
words.example: The class is diverse: people from many countries.

words.definition: An idea thought to be true, but not yet proven.
words.example: The scientist made a hypothesis before the experiment.

words.definition: An explanation for why things happen, based on evidence.
words.example: The theory explains why it rains.

words.definition: Something that happens in nature and can be observed.
words.example: A rainbow is a phenomenon that happens when it rains and the sun shines.

words.definition: All the living things and the place where they live together.
words.example: The forest is an ecosystem with trees, animals, and insects.

words.definition: The wide variety of plants and animals in a place.
words.example: The rainforest has great biodiversity: thousands of different species.

words.definition: The kind of weather a place usually has over a long time.
words.example: Spain's climate is warm in summer.

words.definition: Machines and tools that help make things easier to do.
words.example: A mobile phone is an example of technology.

words.definition: Works with computers or screens, not on paper.
words.example: Now many procedures are done digitally.

words.definition: Brings something new that didn't exist before.
words.example: That invention is innovative: no one had made it before.

words.definition: When countries around the world become more connected and alike.
words.example: Globalization makes it easy to buy things from other countries.

words.definition: Everything important from the past that belongs to a place, like buildings or customs.
words.example: The cathedral is part of the city's heritage.

words.definition: A large group of people living in an organized way, with rules and culture.
words.example: The Romans were a great civilization.

words.definition: A way of thinking about life and its big questions.
words.example: Philosophy tries to answer what happiness is.

words.definition: What is thought to be right or wrong to do.
words.example: For ethics, a doctor should never lie to a patient.

words.definition: Known because it has been tested, not just imagined.
words.example: The result is empirical: it was checked several times in the lab.

words.definition: Based on real facts, not on what someone feels.
words.example: The referee must be objective and not favour any team.

words.definition: Depends on what each person thinks or feels.
words.example: Whether a film is good is subjective.

words.definition: Cannot be touched or seen, it is an idea.
words.example: Freedom is an abstract concept.

words.definition: Clear and real, not a vague idea.
words.example: Give me a concrete example of what you mean.

words.definition: Something that seems impossible or contradictory, but can be true.
words.example: It's a paradox: the faster you run on the treadmill, the less you move forward.

words.definition: Comparing two different things because they are alike in some way.
words.example: He explained the heart with an analogy: it's like a water pump.

words.definition: Closed completely, letting nothing in or out.
words.example: The jar is airtight: no air gets in or out.

words.definition: Complicated and advanced, made with great care.
words.example: That device is sophisticated: it has many functions.

words.definition: Originally from the place where it lives, not from elsewhere.
words.example: The lynx is a native animal of Spain.

words.definition: True or understood everywhere, by everyone.
words.example: Music is a universal language.
